title: U.S. House · Florida's 26th District
area: Western Miami-Dade and Collier counties, including Hialeah, Doral, part of the Everglades, and Naples-area communities.

context.text: Both major-party primaries were canceled: incumbent Mario Diaz-Balart advanced unopposed as the Republican nominee, and Nicole Locklin advanced unopposed as the Democratic nominee (after Yurina Gil, Dustin Lapolla and Robyn Elaine Lawrence did not make the ballot). Deborah Meidinger Hosey is running with No Party Affiliation.

candidates.name: Mario Diaz-Balart
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from a canceled Republican primary, unopposed.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative, Florida's 26th District (since 2023); in Congress since 2003

summary.text: Mario Diaz-Balart is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election in Florida's 26th District. He has served in the U.S. House continuously since 2003 (under different district numbers due to redistricting) and previously served in the Florida State Senate and Florida House.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of South Florida.
Served in the Florida State Senate (District 37) from 1992 to 2000, and the Florida House of Representatives (District 112) from 2000 to 2002, before being elected to the U.S. House in 2002.

record.text: Serves as Vice Chair of the House Committee on Appropriations and chairs its Subcommittee on National Security, Department of State and Related Programs, in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Chaired the Appropriations Subcommittee on State Department and Foreign Operations during the 118th Congress (2023-2024).

candidates.researchNotes: Diaz-Balart has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; his federal key votes and FEC finance totals are added separately by script, per this project's division of labor.

candidates.name: Nicole Locklin
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from a canceled Democratic primary, unopposed.

summary.text: Nicole Locklin is the Democratic nominee for Florida's 26th District. She is an attorney who has practiced in litigation, technology, healthcare, privacy and artificial intelligence law, and is running on affordability and anti-corruption themes.

background.text: Graduated from Pond Creek-Hunter High School in Oklahoma, and says she was the first in her family to graduate from college; earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Oklahoma (2009) and a law degree from Santa Clara University School of Law (2015).
Worked for more than a decade as an attorney in litigation, technology, healthcare, privacy and artificial-intelligence law.

priorities.text: Affordability: lowering costs for housing, insurance, groceries, childcare and healthcare, which she attributes to what she calls government corruption favoring corporations.
Government accountability: banning congressional stock trading, overturning Citizens United, exposing dark money and strengthening ethics rules; she says she does not accept corporate PAC money.
Tax fairness: closing tax loopholes and raising taxes on very high wealth and corporate profits to fund healthcare, Social Security, Medicare, childcare and education.

positions.summary: Says she will close tax loopholes, reduce or eliminate income taxes on working families, and make billionaires and profitable corporations pay a fairer share.
positions.quote: I will close those loopholes, reduce or eliminate income taxes on working families, tax extreme wealth and income fairly, and make profitable corporations contribute to the country that made their success possible.

positions.summary: Says she wants to use revenue from tax fairness measures to guarantee healthcare for every American and strengthen Medicare and Social Security.
positions.quote: We should use that revenue to guarantee healthcare for every American, lower prescription costs, strengthen Medicare and Social Security, support childcare and education, and invest in America's future.

positions.summary: Lists investing in childcare and education among the priorities she would fund through tax-fairness measures.

candidates.researchNotes: Locklin has not previously held elected office, so has no official voting or bill-sponsorship record; positions are drawn from her 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey.
